blocks.label: Shot 1
blocks.body: Medium shot, slow dolly in. A retired boxer taping his hands in a basement gym. He finishes taping, flexes the fist. Basement gym at 6am, condensation on the windows. Practical lamps only. Crushed blacks, high contrast grade. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Shot 2
blocks.body: Medium shot, arc around subject. Looks up at the camera. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Shot 3
blocks.body: Medium shot, handheld follow. Looks up at the camera. 3 seconds.

blocks.label: Audio
blocks.body: He says, "Last round." SFX: skipping rope on concrete. Ambient: distant traffic.

settings.name: Frame rate
settings.why: 48 or 50 for high motion and PAL

settings.name: Audio
settings.why: Generated with the video, not dubbed after

notes: LTX Studio is built around a shot list and @Element references, so Forge writes per-shot rather than one paragraph.
Retake regenerates a 2–16 second segment without a full reshoot. It is the correct fix for one bad beat.
The 48 and 50fps options are a real differentiator for sports and for PAL broadcast conform.
warnings: @Element tags only resolve inside LTX Studio projects. They are meaningless in a raw LTX-2 API call.
Free use is capped by a revenue threshold, not by feature. Check it before commercial deployment.

variations.name: Colder, more documentary
variations.text: Swap the grade for desaturated earth tones, drop to available light only, and shoot it on a 35mm at f/2.8. Same subject, no styling.

variations.name: Tighter and more graphic
variations.text: Go to an extreme close-up on the single most telling detail. Hard directional light, deep shadow, generous negative space around it.

variations.name: Wider, with context
variations.text: Pull back to an establishing wide. Put the subject small in the frame and let the setting carry the story. Keep the same light and grade.
